claimAdmission.rule: when any comparative or promotion claim is admitted, including one from a screening (P-SCREEN) run, the verdict comes only from the evaluator's own QUALIFICATION_RUN at the claimed commit (RULINGS Q55a); records an experiment or the claimant supplies, never from supplied case names or Booleans, are diagnostics only. The evaluator builds the declared tree and requires: a passing G7.position.coordinates run for that build and composition over POSITION_REQUIRED_CASES; G10.composition.identity-bound with every assignment bound (engine, image digest, configuration hash, slot) and the source's protocol variant declared, a log source binding its log identity and durability configuration (RULINGS Q55b); where any claimed obligation uses O-DOMAIN, the W0 pin accepted through VERIFIER_REGISTRY, the O-DOMAIN fingerprint pinned by a reviewed contract version (never from the claim, RULINGS Q55e) and a passing W0.coverage-floors run; every oracle the claim or its prerequisites use pinned and accepted through VERIFIER_REGISTRY, with the claimed obligation outside that pin's excludes and refusals. Cases are resolved from the pinned manifests, every case in every mode; expected answers come from running the pinned oracle, so an oracle exit 2 or X-NOT-MODELED never counts as PASS; the declared comparator decides. The control is A0 from the A0_REGISTRY entry for the claim's source engine, rebuilt by the evaluator to the registry's binarySha256 and run on the same evaluator-chosen workload (WORKLOAD_IDENTITY) as paired rounds, each arm on its own registered slot and placement (RULINGS Q46b, Q47b, Q60, Q67g); a promotion claim is rejected explicitly until its prerequisites are enforced (RULINGS Q67j); while that entry is null every comparison is a diagnostic. Independent verification of the claimed obligation counts only through a VERIFIER_REGISTRY entry for that obligation and commit. Unknown obligation ids are rejected, never dropped. lab/bin/claim.mjs implements this (EXP-E01) with these functions as the reference model. A claim with a failed or pending prerequisite is a diagnostic, never a qualified winner; while O-REPLAY's pin is null every claim is a diagnostic, and A0 measurements may run and produce diagnostics, never closures (RULINGS Q34d, Q37b, Q38b)

commitOutcomes.variantRule: every composition declares its source implementation and protocol variant (RULINGS Q55b): log-source (a host log or broker is the source of truth and an engine is its replica: the QLever lane's broker (C2), EXP-P2Q's host log, and XTDB behind the host log in EXP-P2B) or engine-source (the engine is the source: XTDB's native commit path); each variant has its own witnessed transition table and the composition's declared variant selects it
commitOutcomes.witnessRule: The expected outcome after a fault is chosen from the last transition with durable or engine-side evidence observed by the fault injector after the crash (the log file's records read back, the engine's committed transactions, the publication marker), never from the system's own claim. A transition the protocol declares but the receipt does not witness fails the case.

comparators.CMP-DIAGNOSTICS: the set of {file, line, column, code} diagnostics equals the expected set exactly
comparators.CMP-ERROR: An expected error matches when the observed error's _tag equals the pinned tag and its reason equals the pinned reason (or one of the listed alternatives for multi-reason ids, the case names which), the original cause is retained, and no rows are returned. Any other error, a success, or partial rows is a FAIL.
comparators.CMP-EXACT-VALUE: typed values equal: integers exactly, decimals by exact value and declared scale, binary64 bit patterns (sign of zero included), text codepoints, datetime instants, json canonical text plus original key order where the case says so
comparators.CMP-ORDERED-ROWS: sequences of canonical rows equal, order included
comparators.CMP-PAGES: the page sequence equals the expected sequence: same rows per page, no duplicate or skipped row, same returned basis on every page
comparators.CMP-SET-ROWS: sorted unique canonical rows equal (packet runner semantics: runner.ts:900-912)

comparisonRules.rule: same family: exact comparison (integer as integers, binary64 by IEEE value, text by Unicode codepoint sequence, datetime by instant, boolean false < true, ref by id codepoints)
an untyped numeric constant compares by numeric value with number and datetime values (number 7 and datetime 7 both equal 7); text '7' is not equal
comparisonRules.source: testkit 'datalog equality predicates compare numeric values as numbers' (packages/testkit/src/index.ts:721)

comparisonRules.rule: integer versus number: equality is false and they never share a group; an ordered comparison across them is preflight E-MIXED-FAMILY unless converted explicitly
comparisonRules.source: RULINGS Q8d (core silent for stored integer versus number)

comparisonRules.rule: every comparison between decimal and integer or number, equality included, and any grouping or set operation mixing them, is a preflight E-MIXED-FAMILY unless the query converts explicitly (DECIMAL_CONVERSIONS); there is no false or null result
every ordered comparison across type families is a preflight E-MIXED-FAMILY, never false; equality across families is false except where a ruling makes it an error (decimal, CMP-DECIMAL-CROSS)
entity ids and ref identities compare only with text or ref constants; a numeric or boolean constant is never equal and != is true
comparisonRules.source: testkit 'datalog equality keeps identity bindings string-typed'

comparisonRules.rule: an untyped string constant matches string and ref values; a typed ref constant matches only ref values
comparisonRules.source: testkit 'datalog untyped strings match string and ref values while typed refs stay exact'

comparisonRules.rule: boolean true and integer 1 are distinct values and distinct groups
comparisonRules.source: packet oracle identity() (event_oracles.py: bool true vs i64 one)

comparisonRules.rule: -0.0 and +0.0 are one value for identity, grouping and set membership; when supports differ only in representation, the returned representation is the one from the support with the lowest (recordedPosition, operation index) (amended by RULINGS Q21 AMB-08; assertion ids are generated per lane and are never used); a single-assertion read returns the stored representation

composition.ackOwnership: the source of truth sends the ACK after its own publication; read-your-own-write holds by routing (the pull at the returned position goes to an eligible index, else the fallback); in normal operation the current index is kept synchronous so the fast path serves that pull; during a current-index outage commits and ACKs continue, pulls fall back, the index catches up from the feed through a bounded queue, and fallback share and recovery time are measured (GS.04b); history and analytics stay asynchronous behind watermarks (RULINGS Q31e, replacing Q28's ACK clause)
composition.basis: a basis is a source-of-truth position (POSITION coordinates (stream, epoch, offset, ordinal)) plus a valid time
composition.brokerCurrentIndex: a broker-side current-entity index (the per-subject current document served from the host, QLever kept for history and analytics) is a candidate current-index layer for P4; EXP-Q05 builds and measures it (RULINGS Q50a)
composition.brokerPromotion: before a log-source composition becomes a default it must close G7.broker.promotion-hardening: an overlay memory bound with backpressure (typed E-OVERLOADED beyond the bound) for replica outages of the GS.04b kind (RULINGS Q50d), and the SQLite substrate of RULINGS Q58c (replacing Q50d's segment rotation and file-lock items) with log erasure by crypto-shredding (RULINGS Q58e); an out-of-process broker and off-device copies are deferred; merging a broker behind a default-off option needs only the Q62a fixes, independently re-verified (RULINGS Q62b)

currentPath.expired: facts whose valid_to has passed retire from the current structure through a valid-time horizon; EXP-P4 measures the 20% expired path (RULINGS Q68e)
currentPath.horizon: the default H trails head by one hour of positions (the 15% basis bucket); a pinned sweep or reconcile holds H at or below its pin; the broker refuses a new pin that would make H trail head by more than 24 hours (RULINGS Q68b)

composition.eligibility: index I is eligible to serve basis B only when all hold: its watermark (a fully resolved prefix) has reached B in B's epoch; C1's eligibility for the query (mapping, valid time, exact cut); I can actually reconstruct B (a current-only index only when B is at or after the last change to every attribute the read touches, the validity interval of R18); and I has applied every erasure published so far, independently of B (ERASURE frontier) (RULINGS Q31d)
composition.engines: each assignment is XTDB or QLever

experimentDirections.EXP-P2B: XTDB as a second replica behind the broker: one pgwire transaction per frame (ASSERT the marker, INSERT rows with a fixed _valid_from, INSERT the new marker; P0004 on guard failure); rows and marker read in one read-only transaction; the marker row is the eligibility authority; XTDB system time never carries broker positions; Local log first, InMemory log plus an epoch bump as an arm; predictions and measurements per R23 section 6; it starts after the Q62a fix round is re-verified, from the same author, so one writer owns the broker files (RULINGS Q58b; Q51b's original direction stays pending)
experimentDirections.EXP-P4: provisional (RULINGS Q68a, Q68g): P4's fast path is one current structure holding live facts plus facts retired after a retention horizon H, served at basis B only when H <= B <= W (W its applied watermark), else the history path; its first copy lives in the broker, written with the frame (arm H1); engines get a smaller copy in the same transaction or guarded update (XTDB tx_current, QLever cur graph) for list and native queries; EXP-P4 measures arms A0, X1, X2, Q1 and H1 per R24 section 6, exactness gate first, and measures X1 (default temporal bounds) fresh and aged before any write-path change, because FOR ALL VALID_TIME on XTDB current reads forfeits the engine's current and historical split
experimentDirections.P1-replicas: read scaling on both lanes comes from replicas fed by the broker (Q58b): each XTDB or QLever replica has its own applier and marker, so readers never touch the writer's log or indexer and the shared-log follower is unnecessary; EXP-P2B measures the first XTDB replica and a second-replica arm follows; Kafka (E8, about 7 GiB) is deferred (RULINGS Q63b)
experimentDirections.broker-hardening: after EXP-P2B: the host log moves to SQLite through better-sqlite3 (WAL, synchronous=FULL, fullfsync=ON, checkpoint_fullfsync=ON, locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE, application-driven PASSIVE checkpoints, a worker thread when readers share the process), keeping a CRC32C prev-chain column, a committed_at column, an epoch row and the marker and checkpoint cross-checks (plain SQLite misses mid-WAL corruption); heads, claims and operations become tables; the overlay becomes a persisted recent_rows table; predictions H1 to H6 of R23 section 6.4 (RULINGS Q58c)

composition.fallbackEquivalence: outage read-your-own-write is tested on every serving surface the composition claims, native surfaces included, each against its readGuarantees guarantee (RULINGS Q55c); a stale fallback is rejected; where a fallback answers in another language, both recipes are bound to one semantic query identity (parameters, basis, meaning) and one expected answer from the oracle; total request latency and language attribution stay recorded (RULINGS Q34b)
composition.hotSubjects: a per-subject FIFO queue in the candidate's command router (bounded; the typed E-OVERLOADED beyond the bound, never an unbounded wait) with same-subject group commit (up to 8 queued commands of one subject in one engine transaction, positions by ordinal); optimistic compare-and-set stays for cross-node races; the queue is part of the candidate, never the driver (RULINGS Q51a)
composition.incarnationFencing: single-request read surfaces read the replica marker in the same request as the answer; multi-request surfaces (Datalog, executor) use replica incarnation fencing: every replay begins by writing a new incarnation id, and an answer is accepted only if (incarnation, marker) is equal before and after (RULINGS Q67c)
composition.layerSwaps: layers are swapped one at a time under matched workloads at small rungs (current-index candidates on P1 and P4; history candidates on past-basis reads and GS.12; source candidates on P2 and P3); only the two or three best compositions go on to end-to-end validation with the golden scenarios
composition.overlay: the overlay merge is allowed for entity pulls only, keyed by id with the greater LSN winning, under a tested invariant (identity columns never change; a retraction is a new version); engine aggregates, Datalog and executor reads and paged lists never merge: they wait or fail typed; frames carry explicit tombstones, so erasure and deletes cannot resurrect replica rows (RULINGS Q58d)
composition.parameterisedSql: seeders and appliers on XTDB use parameterised statements only; 1,000-row literal INSERTs exhausted a 2 GiB heap (EXP-X05), as per-cell expressions did in EXP-P2X (RULINGS Q63d)

readGuarantees.honesty: no surface may present an answer as at a basis it was not computed at
readGuarantees.native: PROVISIONAL, flagged for Sam (RULINGS Q58a, superseding Q55c's native half): native SPARQL, XTQL, SQL and Datalog go through a Triplex facade; engine ports are not a public surface. A request may carry after: position (wait until the replica marker reaches it within the deadline, then the typed E-BASIS-NOT-AVAILABLE {required, observed, replica}) or at: position (exact; the engine must also reconstruct it, else the typed E-BASIS-NOT-RECONSTRUCTIBLE). A client session sends its own high-water mark (its last commit position and last read basis) as an implicit after. A tokenless external caller gets the replica's watermark and the reported position. Every answer carries {basis: {low, high}, route}. With the replica unreachable the answer is the typed E-REPLICA-UNAVAILABLE. The default deadline is 2 s
readGuarantees.repository: repository pulls give read-your-own-write by routing (replica, else overlay, else the source's log), never below the caller's basis; with the replica unreachable they fall back to the source (RULINGS Q50a)
readGuarantees.status: PROVISIONAL, flagged for Sam (RULINGS Q55c, superseding Q50b; the native half is replaced by Q58a)
readGuarantees.testing: NS.P2 and G7.composition.ack-and-routed-ryow test each surface the composition claims against its own guarantee; NS.P2's repository read-your-own-write never establishes a native-surface guarantee

composition.receiptBinding: every receipt binds, per assignment, the engine image digest, configuration hash and slot; every replication edge (feed consumer source hash, translation generation); and each serving index's watermark at read time
composition.scopeKey: an engine-scope receipt's key is (layer, the engine assigned to that layer, its image digest, configuration hash and slot), derived from the composition, never from engineOfLane
composition.sharedVolumeFollower: rejected for promotion: XTDB 2.2.0's ReadOnlyLocalLog reads half-written records and dies permanently (9 deaths in 30 minutes), though it never answered wrongly; the second-writer guard and the follower harness stay; the torn-read repro joins the R21 upstream-filing question for Sam, and nothing is filed without him (RULINGS Q63a, Q63c)
composition.sourceDeclaration: every composition declares its source implementation: the source assignment carries variant engine-source or log-source (COMMIT_OUTCOMES), and a log source binds its log identity and durability configuration (implementationSha256, fsyncMode, fullFsync, device; LOG_FIELDS) next to the engine identities in every receipt (RULINGS Q55b)
composition.watermarkRouting: a read that finds no eligible index waits at most T-WATERMARK-WAIT-MS for one, then routes to an eligible fallback (the source of truth's own query surface or another index); the fallback's latency counts in the read's own latency; the receipt records the route and the surface language, a cross-language fallback is counted per surface, and fallbacks are reported as a share of reads per window; no index answers for a basis it is not eligible for (RULINGS Q31d)

constraintRules.rule: with enforcement on, a command is rejected only when its post-state creates a new violation or worsens an existing one at some represented valid-time boundary; a pre-existing violation does not block an unrelated command and stays readable
write-time cardinality counts live assertions, including equal-valued duplicates (unchanged)
a card-one conflict that predates the enforcing write stays a conflict (C5.2) and reads per C5.3

conversionRules.rule: toNumber(integer): round to nearest binary64, ties to even, once
toInteger(number): only explicit; the value must be integral and inside integer, else E-INVALID-CONVERSION; -0.0 converts to 0
CAST text to integer: canonical decimal only (optional leading '-', no '+', no leading zeros except '0', no '-0'), inside integer, else E-INVALID-CONVERSION or E-INTEGER-OVERFLOW
no implicit conversion between families anywhere (filters, joins, group keys, aggregates)

cursorTransitions.retention: No retention policy exists, so 'cut no longer retained' is never a permitted outcome.
cursorTransitions.rule: A cursor or a requested historical basis issued before any transition below continues successfully afterward (through the exact ledger path where the projection changed), returning exactly the rows O-REPLAY computes at the cursor's basis. An available retained cut never becomes unavailable because its projection, mapping or index changed.

decimalConversions.rule: integer to decimal(p, s): exact when the integer fits p - s digits, else E-DECIMAL-OVERFLOW

decimal to integer (toInteger): only when the fraction is zero, else E-DECIMAL-FRACTION unless the caller writes round(x, 0, rounding) first; a whole decimal outside the integer range is E-INTEGER-OVERFLOW (RULINGS Q43g)
decimal to number: only through toNumber(x) (named, lossy, one correctly rounded binary64)
number to decimal: only through toDecimal(x, p, s, rounding); NaN and infinities never occur (rejected at write)

text to decimal at the write boundary: the canonical decimal grammar only; more fractional digits than s (counted on the value) is E-DECIMAL-FRACTION and more than p - s integer digits is E-DECIMAL-OVERFLOW, never rounded
no implicit conversion between decimal and integer or number in any expression; mixing them is preflight E-MIXED-FAMILY (CMP-DECIMAL-CROSS)

decimalOps.error: E-DECIMAL-OVERFLOW when the result exceeds the target's declared precision or 38 digits
decimalOps.op: a + b, a - b (decimal(p1, s1), decimal(p2, s2))
decimalOps.resultPrecision: max(p1 - s1, p2 - s2) + max(s1, s2) + 1

decimalOps.error: E-DECIMAL-OVERFLOW when the result exceeds the target's declared precision or 38 digits
E-DIVISION-BY-ZERO for b = 0; E-DECIMAL-OVERFLOW beyond the precision; the one place rounding happens, and only when the caller names it
decimalOps.op: divide(a, b, scale, rounding) with rounding one of half-even, half-up, down

decimalOps.error: E-DECIMAL-OVERFLOW only when a carry exceeds the precision or the 38-digit cap
decimalOps.resultPrecision: p - (s_x - s) when s < s_x; p + (s - s_x), capped at 38, when s > s_x (exact: appends zeros, never refused); p when s = s_x

decimalOps.error: E-DECIMAL-OVERFLOW when the exact total exceeds 38 digits
decimalOps.op: SUM over decimals (kernel; engine side only where a projection needs it)

decimalRouting.rule: repository ORDER BY and range on a decimal attribute use the decimal_order_v1 key
native ORDER BY and range in the lane language use the decimal_order_v1 key, never QLever's lexical canonical text
raw recipes order and range on the documented decimal_order_v1 channel, never the lexical text
a derived decimal expression used for ordering or comparison is computed exactly in the kernel and encoded to TDK1 before it is compared
SUM over decimals decodes the keys or canonical text, computes exactly, and encodes any decimal result used for ordering; MIN and MAX compare keys
arithmetic on key strings (summing or subtracting decimal_order_v1 values as text or numbers) is invalid: preflight E-MIXED-FAMILY
a decimal-looking number inside a JSON value is opaque: it is never compared, ordered or summed as a decimal

an explicit conversion of a JSON number to a typed decimal (toDecimal with declared precision and scale) starts from the number's as-written reading (the read-back-as-written text of RULINGS Q33a), never its exact binary64 expansion, so toDecimal(json 0.1, 2, 1) = 0.1; it validates the result (E-DECIMAL-FRACTION, E-DECIMAL-OVERFLOW or E-INVALID-VALUE) and encodes the TDK1 key (RULINGS Q49e)

decimal text inside a JSON string is E-INVALID-VALUE where a decimal is required, unless the query converts the string explicitly (RULINGS Q49e); the explicitly converted half is a lane obligation, because O-REPLAY does not model text-to-decimal conversion (RULINGS Q66d)

decimalRoutingQ52.rule: toDecimal(json, p, s, rounding) applies the named mode (half-even, half-up or down, Q22) to the JSON number's as-written decimal reading (Q49e); without a rounding argument, excess digits are E-DECIMAL-FRACTION (RULINGS Q52f)

decimalRules.arithmetic: TypeScript kernel, exact decimal arithmetic; engine-side decimal arithmetic only where a projection needs it (RULINGS Q19)
decimalRules.avg: AVG over decimal is preflight E-DECIMAL-AVG unless written as divide(SUM, COUNT, scale, rounding) (R-DEC-7); decimal divide is modeled by the oracle (follow-up EXP-O03, R-DEC-5)
decimalRules.comparison: CMP-DECIMAL-CROSS: comparison with integer or number is preflight E-MIXED-FAMILY unless the query converts explicitly
decimalRules.declaration: every decimal attribute declares precision p (total significant digits) and scale s (fractional digits), 0 <= s <= p
decimalRules.family: decimal is its own family, ordered between number and datetime (CARD_MANY_ORDER); 1.50 and 1.5 are one value
decimalRules.inputCapture: the writer captures the caller's original typed input before any normalization; tests assert nothing was rounded before capture (DEC-INPUT-CAPTURE, M-DECIMAL-PRECAPTURE-ROUND)
decimalRules.oneRepresentation: the decimal kind has exactly one stored representation; Q18's scaled-integer path no longer applies; money modeled as integer cents uses the integer kind (RULINGS Q35b)
decimalRules.reject: a value with more than s fractional digits (counted on the value, so 16.500 fits scale 2, R-DEC-3) fails with E-DECIMAL-FRACTION; a value beyond the declared precision or 38 digits fails with E-DECIMAL-OVERFLOW; -0.00 in any spelling is refused with E-INVALID-VALUE (R-DEC-2); a decimal on an attribute not declared decimal is E-INVALID-VALUE (R-DEC-0); every rejection leaves no residue; never rounded or truncated (RULINGS Q33b, Q35e)

storage.as: the TDK1 key in channel decimal_order_v1 (authoritative, decodes exactly) plus derived canonical text at the declared scale; QLever also keeps its lexical channel for parity with other kinds (RULINGS Q35b, amending Q18)
storage.when: every declared precision and scale (both lanes)

decimalRules.toDecimal: toDecimal(number, p, s, rounding) starts from the number's exact binary expansion, then applies the caller's scale and rounding (R-DEC-6)
decimalRules.wireShape: {"type": "decimal", "value": "16.50"} (R-DEC-1); a value with extra trailing zeros is returned at the declared scale (16.500 at scale 2 reads back as 16.50) while the original input text is still captured (Q22, R-DEC-3)

decimalScaleEvolution.rule: a declaration change that admits every existing value is metadata-only: TDK1 keys depend on the value alone, so Q31g's key-compatibility condition always holds and no key is rewritten; stored values read back with the new declared scale (RULINGS Q35b, superseding Q31g's migration path)

a change under which some existing value no longer fits (for example integer digits p - s shrink) validates every live and historical value first and fails atomically with E-DECIMAL-NARROWING before any mutation; no key rewrite is ever needed
narrowing precision or scale is a migration that fails atomically with E-DECIMAL-NARROWING, before any mutation, if any live or historical value would lose digits

decimalTests.DEC-ADJACENT-LARGE: adjacent 38-digit decimals (differing in the last digit) stay distinct and ordered on every surface
decimalTests.DEC-EVERY-PATH: every query and serialization path (Triples, repository, native, raw hatch, feed, journal, backup and restore) round-trips exactly
decimalTests.DEC-INPUT-CAPTURE: the writer's captured input equals the caller's original typed input before normalization
decimalTests.DEC-INTERMEDIATE: arithmetic intermediates are exact (no rounding before the final result)
decimalTests.DEC-NEGATIVE: negative values, including order across zero
decimalTests.DEC-ORDER-KEY-INDEPENDENT: an independent checker compares the order-key byte order with exact numeric order over the whole CS-DECIMAL corpus
decimalTests.DEC-SCALE-BOUNDARY: values with exactly s fractional digits and exactly p - s integer digits accepted; one more rejected

diagnosticRule: A diagnostic keeps its original text and unchanged expected answer. It runs inside every acceptance run of the obligation that names it, its actual answer is retained, and it never closes or blocks anything. A missing diagnostic execution fails the naming obligation's receipt.

diagnostics.what: original raw text order and range counterexamples: tiny collation control `ORDER BY STR(?l) STR(?e)` and its two ranges; string-order-v1 native raw page; the R5 A3 IRI page-sample class
write 2^59 and 2^63-1 as native xsd:integer through the raw wire and read them back (shows why the Triplex write path must reject these values)
9007199254740993 = 9007199254740992.0 and grouping of integer 1 with number 1.0
original flat and nested correlated NOT EXISTS controls, unedited text
raw SUM over BIGINT of [2^62, 2^62] and [2^62, 2^62, -2^62] in SQL and XTQL
fractional-millisecond datetime read through the node postgres driver

entrypoints.EP-ENGINE-OBS: Engine-side observation only (metrics, logs, active queries, connection lists, container stats).

entrypoints.EP-EXPLAIN: Public plan and route capture for repository queries and native reads.
entrypoints.EP-FEED: The ordered, resumable change feed: entries carry tx, entity, attribute and the valid-time range affected; consumers resume from a checkpoint.
entrypoints.EP-KERNEL: The TypeScript kernel that evaluates rule comparisons and per-subject arithmetic over values read from the store (exact BigInt and decimal arithmetic); the receipt records the exported function.
entrypoints.EP-NATIVE: The lane's native surface with helper fragments: xtdb-xtql `select`, xtdb-sql `selectSql`, qlever-sparql native SPARQL.

Its subject pull is the P4 read shape.

erasure.boundary: the boundary is the erasure commit's publication; a read that started before it sees, for each erasure commit, either all of that commit's values as they were or all as markers, never a mix (RULINGS Q52e, narrowing Q49d); every read that starts after it, at any basis including bases before the erasure, returns ErasedValue {erasedAt} in place of the value
erasure.cacheInvalidation: erasure invalidates every old-basis cache entry that holds the erased value
erasure.commandShape: the op is spelled erase; erasure is a typed invalid-command error; an erase is its own command, and mixing it with other operations or giving it preconditions is a typed invalid-command error (RULINGS Q52g)
erasure.currentCopies: provisional: every current copy (the broker's current store, XTDB tx_current, the QLever cur graph) is covered by Q58e's per-subject keys; a QLever cur graph holds no personal-data literals (keys and references only, values from the encrypted host store) unless EXP-P4 shows a reindex-free erasure path (RULINGS Q68f)
erasure.derivedChannels: a PII attribute's order key and lexical channel are inside the encrypted envelope (range rules on PII then run in the kernel after decryption), or the attribute is not eligible for range rules
erasure.frontier: an index or cache may serve any basis only after it has applied every erasure published so far, independently of the requested basis; an old-basis read never passes on the strength of its basis alone (RULINGS Q31f)
erasure.idempotence: the first erasure of an identity sets erasedAt; erasing it again changes nothing; an erase that matches nothing still commits, as a journal record with an empty change list (RULINGS Q49b)
erasure.inFlight: an erasure commit is atomic for readers: a read that started before it published sees either all of that commit's values as they were or all as markers, never a mix (RULINGS Q52e, narrowing Q49d from per value to per commit); erasure commits become visible in position order, so a read that started before n in-flight erasure commits in its scope sees a prefix of them, and the acceptable answers are the n + 1 prefixes, never all 2^n subsets (RULINGS Q66a); a continuation cursor carries the erasure prefix its page was computed with, and every later page answers with that same prefix (RULINGS Q66b); only erasures in the read's own scope are in flight, erasures in other scopes always apply (RULINGS Q66c)
erasure.journalCommit: an erasure commit is an ordinary data-journal transaction: it has a position, a txId, a record in transactions() and its own :_tx/ facts, and its changes list only identities (entity, attribute, assertion ids), never values; it is also written to the erasure ledger kept apart from the data, which restore and rebuild replay; earlier transactions' :_tx/change facts for erased values show the ErasedValue marker, so ER-JOURNAL-MODULO compares markers on both sides (RULINGS Q49a)
erasure.keyEvidence: for crypto-shredding, the lane's inventory shows that every surviving copy of a protected value, and of anything derived from it, is encrypted only under the destroyed key; deleting some key is not evidence
erasure.logErasure: values held in the broker log, the recent_rows overlay and checkpoints are erasable: value payloads in frames are encrypted per subject and erasure destroys the key (crypto-shredding), so TARGETS 7 holds without rewriting the log; designed in the broker-hardening experiment (RULINGS Q58e)
erasure.presence: an erased value is still a present assertion: a card-one attribute holding a readable and an erased value conflicts with E-CONFLICTING-VALUES as two readable values would, the remedy being to retract the erased assertion (Q56b); answers never depend on the erased value, so a readable SAME beside an erased support conflicts whatever the erased value was (Q56c); in a card-many value list erased markers come after the readable elements, ordered by assertion id (Q56d); Required is satisfied by an erased value (Q56e) (RULINGS Q56, provisional under the Q24 flag)
erasure.queries: provisional, under the Q24 flag for Sam: an erased value is present with no readable value; it matches no value predicate (equality, inequality, range, pattern), so a filter never selects or rejects a subject by it; SUM, AVG, MIN and MAX skip it while COUNT of assertions counts it; ORDER BY places erased markers last in a deterministic order by assertion id; grouping puts all erased values of an attribute in one group keyed by the marker; Unique ignores erased values; an erased reference cannot be followed (an include returns the marker) (RULINGS Q49c)
erasure.queriesResidual: provisional, under the Q24 flag for Sam: a count of distinct values counts an attribute's erased values as one value (the marker group), a count of assertions counts each erased assertion (Q52a); ORDER BY puts readable values first, then erased markers by assertion id, then missing values, in both directions (Q52b); a marker group reports the earliest erasedAt among its members (Q52c); an erased reference takes no part in reference constraints: it blocks no restrict delete, cascades nothing and is skipped by ReferenceTarget validation (Q52d) (RULINGS Q52)
erasure.reproduction: every reproduction contract holds modulo erasure: the C6 whole-journal comparison, raw and native query results, SDK results, cursor stability, bit-for-bit explain and GS.12; both sides of a comparison replace erased values with their markers before comparing (RULINGS Q31f)
erasure.restore: the erasure ledger is kept apart from the data and replayed after any restore or rebuild
erasure.selectors: matches nothing (Q49b) means a well-formed entity or entity-plus-attribute selector with no assertions to erase, which commits with an empty change list; an erase naming an unknown assertion target or an unknown id is E-INVALID-VALUE, as for retract (Q56a); erase accepts the same selectors as retract, including {id: ...} (Q56f); retracting an already erased assertion by target commits and history shows the marker with the retraction's time, so erase then delete is supported (Q56g) (RULINGS Q56)
erasure.shape: assertion identities and valid and record intervals keep their shape
erasure.status: PROVISIONAL product ruling (RULINGS Q24), flagged for Sam: explain at a pre-erasure basis shows the marker, not the value
erasure.syntheticData: in-flight outputs may hold pre-erasure values (Q49d, Q52e), so every oracle case, fixture and golden scenario uses synthetic values only; no real personal data enters the lab (RULINGS Q56h)

build-manifest/1.rule: binds the source tree to the executed binary; the binary and every executed or imported module ({path, sha256}, at least one) are retained objects whose bytes hash to the listed values

build-manifest/2.rule: build-manifest/1 plus the build inputs ({path, sha256}, every one checked against the side's commit) and the hash of the contract's BUILD_SPEC (RULINGS Q61f)

case-result/1.rule: the retained raw oracle run and observation for one case and the selection it covers; PASS only when oracleExit is 0, oracleCode is null, the expected and observed objects are both retained and equal; an oracle exit 2 or X-NOT-MODELED is a refusal and never PASS (RULINGS Q45b, Q47a)

case-result/2.rule: case-result/1 plus the mode, the repetition, the comparator applied and the input's sha256; a run that cannot be expressed in this record fails closed (RULINGS Q61e); a case reached by several select entries records the first select entry in contract order (RULINGS Q65c); its verdict is recomputed with its declared comparator on the retained raw objects, never by hash equality (RULINGS Q67i, Q71c)

fault-witness/1.rule: one retained record per fault injection (the injector's point and time, the last transition with durable evidence, and the retained transition events), never a faultReps count alone (RULINGS Q61j; EVIDENCE_KINDS fault-witness)

oracle-invocation/1.rule: one record per oracle invocation, with the runtime that ran it (for a Python oracle, its version), because an answer can depend on it (RULINGS Q71b)

verifier-record/1.rule: names the receipt's obligation and definition hash, a nonempty verifier and the verdict ACCEPT

frontierRules.accounting: A task whose host steps are only HS-FRONTIER (and HS-NORMALIZE) operations counts as pure in the lane's language.
frontierRules.bounds: maxRounds and maxRecursiveRows are declared per task. Reaching a bound fails with the typed recursion-limit error (ERROR_TABLE E-RECURSION-LIMIT) and returns no partial answer.
frontierRules.cost: Host frontier time and peak host memory are counted inside the task's measured cost and reported per round.
frontierRules.fixedCut: Every round runs at the same captured basis (scope, P, optional R, V); each round's trace records that basis and the evaluator checks they are identical.
forbiddenHostOperations: filtering on values, types, entity types or time
negation, aggregation, ordering or pagination of answers
any read that does not go through the lane's native language
frontierRules.noMutation: No round writes engine state (engine-side mutation count unchanged across the read).
permittedHostOperations: subtract the visited set from the new frontier
test termination (empty frontier, maxRounds reached, maxRecursiveRows reached)
bind the next frontier as query parameters, chunked so each native query stays within its declared parameter bound
count rows and rounds against the bounds

goldenRule: The golden JSON files stay unchanged as the audit record (RULINGS Q29a). A golden-vector query whose expected answer reads AMBIGUOUS is evaluated with the reading named in GOLDEN_RESOLUTIONS (plus its refinement, if any); the other readings stay in the file as the audit record. For AMB-01 the original tiny-v4 target answers also close on repository as-of reads, timeline and native history (RS-RAW-LIFETIME). The golden files are pinned by sha256 in obligations.json; a changed file needs a contract version.
goldenScenarioRules: A seeded, deterministic generator produces the command stream and the reads; the same seed gives the same bytes.

Expected answers come from the independent oracles, never from a system under test: O-REPLAY for database state and values, O-DOMAIN for domain outputs and effects under WORLD_W0, or a frozen hand derivation with a citation (O-HAND).
A scenario's commands are overlaid on the background trace, never instead of it; the receipt accounts for both streams separately.
Every scenario carries positive witnesses (subjects that must change, GS-nn-WITNESS-POS) and negative witnesses (subjects that must not, GS-nn-WITNESS-NEG).
Plan-impact preview (GS.11) and activation (GS.10) are compared at one common input basis (GS-10-11-COMMON-BASIS).
The added failure schedules of GS_FAILURE_SCHEDULES (TARGETS 6.1) are named cases of their scenario and must meet their expected outcome.

Each GS obligation binds only its own scenario: it selects its own tag and named cases, names exactly its own bars plus T-RUNS, and its receipt carries an ns-run whose measurement is its own scenario id (RULINGS Q26).
Unless a scenario says otherwise it runs on P-YEAR-ONE with the fixed writer trace running and 256 concurrent pinned readers (P-NS).

A scenario fails on any wrong answer, any lost or duplicated commit, any feed gap or order violation, or any missed bar; its receipt records the correctness verdicts and the P1 to P5 measurements together.
All 20 run on every composition being compared, and the final acceptance reruns all 20 fresh.

Numbers inside the scenarios: pay rates, hours and money use integer cents (the integer kind) or the decimal kind (TDK1 key); the scenarios include the range rules 'pay rate at or above 16.50' and 'hours over 40' (cases GS-NUM-RANGE-1650 and GS-NUM-HOURS-40, selected by GS.18's dashboard filters) and at least one write of a value the lane cannot hold, which must fail with E-VALUE-OUT-OF-RANGE, E-DECIMAL-OVERFLOW or E-DECIMAL-FRACTION (GS-NUM-UNHOLDABLE, selected by GS.02).

legacyRule: Follow-up EXP-G02 (RULINGS Q32b): QLever in-range companion vectors by an independent golden author. modeRule: Every obligation declares at least one mode. 'single-execution' runs each selected case once, so executions equal selections; NS and GS obligations use it explicitly (RULINGS Q26). 'paired-rounds' (NS obligations, RULINGS Q60f) runs every comparison under PAIR_0: paired rounds of A0 and candidate, never a single run. Other modes (current, reopen, engine-restart) each run every selected case once more.
mutantRule: A mutant counts only when (1) its reach probe fired at least once during a targeted case, and (2) at least one targeted case failed through a comparator mismatch on an identified assertion (case id and assertion id), not through an error, timeout, crash or setup failure. Mutants patch only the system under test; oracle, case and gate hashes are identical to the clean receipt.

obligations.statement: Per COMPOSITION brokerPromotion (RULINGS Q50d), for a log-source composition: the overlay has a memory bound with backpressure, so a replica outage of the GS.04b kind returns the typed E-OVERLOADED beyond the bound and never grows without limit (BR-OVERLAY-BOUND-OVERLOADED); per RULINGS Q58c, replacing Q50d's rotation and lock items, the log is SQLite through better-sqlite3 with WAL, synchronous=FULL, fullfsync=ON, checkpoint_fullfsync=ON, locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE and application-driven PASSIVE checkpoints, a second writer being refused (BR-SQLITE-DURABILITY-PRAGMAS); a CRC32C prev-chain column detects mid-WAL corruption plain SQLite misses (BR-CRC-CHAIN-MID-WAL); every frame records committed_at (BR-COMMITTED-AT); an epoch row closes the previous epoch (BR-EPOCH-ROW); the marker and checkpoint are cross-checked against the log on open (BR-MARKER-CHECKPOINT-CROSSCHECK); the overlay is the persisted recent_rows table (BR-RECENT-ROWS-PERSISTED); and per RULINGS Q58e value payloads in frames, recent_rows and checkpoints are encrypted per subject, so erasure destroys the key (BR-LOG-CRYPTO-SHRED).
obligations.title: A log-source composition is hardened before promotion

obligations.statement: With the frozen writer trace running, closed-loop readers at 1, 4, 16, 64 and 256 (and 1,024 stress) each name their basis (valid time and record time or tx), in the lane's language, under TARGETS 1.1 P1: readers and writers share one hot set (at least half the reads target subjects written in the previous 60 s, NS-P1-HOT-SET); 10% of subgraph reads are split into two or more queries at the same named basis, scheduled to straddle a command the frozen trace already holds for that subject (step 1 before its ACK, step 2 after), and must equal the oracle at the requested basis (NS-P1-SPLIT-READ); the driver adds no writes of its own, so faster readers never change the write load (NS-P1-SPLIT-NO-DRIVER-WRITES, RULINGS Q31b); every window contains at least one maintenance event (NS-P1-MAINTENANCE-IN-WINDOW); the driver records the requested basis itself and the verifier checks answers at it (NS-P1-DRIVER-BASIS); reader-caused writer waits are attributed by matched-phase comparison against the zero-reader run and by engine-side wait evidence where the engine exposes it (NS-P1-WAIT-ATTRIBUTION). Every NS-P1-* bar holds: zero violations, goodput at 256 not below 64, read p99 within NS-P1-READ-P99-256-MS, writer commit p99 within NS-P1-WRITER-P99-RATIO-256 of its zero-reader baseline, no command waits beyond NS-P1-WRITER-WAIT-MAX-MS, and at 1,024 goodput within NS-P1-GOODPUT-1024-VS-256, writer p99 within NS-P1-WRITER-P99-RATIO-1024, back to the 256-level bar within NS-P1-RECOVERY-MS.

obligations.statement: Open loop under TARGETS 1.1 P2: commands are offered on the frozen schedule and latency runs from the scheduled offer to the published ACK (sent only once the commit is durable and readable), so queueing behind other writers counts. The trace's own commands are reported per size band: the 5-to-10 band (NS-P2-BAND-5-10) and the 11-to-25 band (NS-P2-BAND-11-25) each meet NS-P2-COMMIT-P50-MS and NS-P2-COMMIT-P99-MS, the 26-to-50 band (NS-P2-BAND-26-50) meets NS-P2-COMMIT-P99-26-50-MS, all with P1's 256 readers running; the 10-fact probe is a diagnostic only. Every offered command is committed with a receipt, rejected with a typed error, or a typed conflict (NS-P2-UNACCOUNTED-MAX, NS-P2-ACCOUNTING), and accounting is not progress: every oracle-valid trace command publishes; typed rejections count only for the trace's deliberately invalid commands and typed conflicts only where the oracle independently finds a compare-and-set race (NS-P2-UNJUSTIFIED-OUTCOMES-MAX, NS-P2-PROGRESS); queued commands never exceed NS-P2-QUEUE-MAX-S of the offered rate at steady state (NS-P2-QUEUE-BOUND) and the queue drains within NS-P2-BURST-DRAIN-S after each burst (NS-P2-BURST-DRAIN) (RULINGS Q31a). The pull at the returned tx sees the commit every time with no extra wait (NS-P2-RYOW-FRACTION), and each serving surface the composition claims is measured against its COMPOSITION readGuarantees guarantee (NS-P2-RYOW-PER-SURFACE, RULINGS Q55c, provisional): repository read-your-own-write never stands in for a native-surface guarantee; hot subjects go through the candidate's bounded per-subject queue with same-subject group commit, and an E-OVERLOADED beyond its bound counts against NS-P2-UNJUSTIFIED-OUTCOMES-MAX, never as progress (NS-P2-HOT-SUBJECT-QUEUE, RULINGS Q51a); duplicates and lost ACKs return the original receipt every time (NS-P2-DUP-RECEIPT-FRACTION).

obligations.statement: Under TARGETS 1.1 P3: feed entries carry tx, entity, attribute and the valid-time range affected; lag runs from the source's own publication timestamp for each position (the broker's durable watermark update, or the engine's commit resolution when the engine is the source), recorded by the source on the shared host monotonic clock independently of ACK delivery, to the consumer's durable record, and every committed position is accounted: none is dropped for a missing ACK, and a missing one is counted and fails the run (NS-P3-EVERY-POSITION-ACCOUNTED, RULINGS Q55d); an ACK-to-consumer figure (such as EXP-P2Q's) is not this measurement until recomputed; both arms enumerate the final published source prefix from the source's own record and timestamp actual publication (the broker's watermark publication, or commit resolution when the engine is the source), ACK records being reconciled afterwards, so a late or lost ACK is never a feed defect (NS-P3-SOURCE-PREFIX-ENUMERATED, RULINGS Q67d; manifest null until built); the cursor is (epoch, position); the expected affected-subject set per transaction is the directly written subjects (O-REPLAY) plus the subjects whose WORLD_W0 static read set contains a changed fact (O-DOMAIN, NS-P3-DOMAIN-AFFECTED-SET, RULINGS Q36e); 'affected subjects known' is the consumer's single durable write of the set and its checkpoint. Over a run there are zero gaps (NS-P3-GAPS-MAX) and zero per-subject order violations (NS-P3-ORDER-VIOLATIONS-MAX); lag stays within NS-P3-LAG-P99-MS with P1's 256 readers running; delivery is at-least-once from the last checkpoint with effects keyed by (consumer, position, subject), so crashes before the effect, after the effect before the checkpoint, and after the checkpoint (NS-P3-CRASH-BEFORE-EFFECT, NS-P3-CRASH-AFTER-EFFECT, NS-P3-CRASH-AFTER-CHECKPOINT) leave zero visible duplicate effects (NS-P3-VISIBLE-DUP-EFFECTS-MAX) while replay attempts are counted separately; resume from a checkpoint replays exactly.

obligations.statement: Every CS-ERASURE boundary, marker and reproduction case per ERASURE: a read that started before the erasure published sees each erasure commit whole, all old values or all markers (ER-INFLIGHT-READ covers a commit erasing one value, identical under Q49d and Q52e; a commit erasing several is G9.erasure.residual-shapes' ER-INFLIGHT-ALL-OR-NONE, RULINGS Q52e); every read that starts after it, at any basis including bases before the erasure, returns ErasedValue {erasedAt} in place of the value (ER-AFTER-PUBLICATION-ALL-BASES), with assertion identities and valid and record intervals unchanged (ER-SHAPE-KEPT); a reader already pinned when the erasure lands follows the same rule (ER-PINNED-READER); an index or cache serves any basis only after applying every published erasure, independently of the basis (ER-FRONTIER-OLD-BASIS), and erasure invalidates every old-basis cache entry holding the value (ER-CACHE-INVALIDATION); expected post-erasure answers come independently from O-REPLAY (ER-ORACLE-POST).
obligations.title: Erasure is a visibility boundary at the erasure commit's publication

obligations.statement: Each lane keeps a protected-copy inventory covering every PROTECTED_COPY_INVENTORY location, a log-source composition's log frames, recent_rows overlay and checkpoints included, which erase by crypto-shredding (ER-LOG-CRYPTO-SHRED, RULINGS Q58e); after the erasure publishes, OBS-ERASURE-SCAN finds no plaintext and no derived-channel copy in any of them, or, for crypto-shredding, evidence that every surviving copy of the value and of anything derived from it is encrypted only under the destroyed per-subject key (ER-KEY-EXCLUSIVE; deleting some key is not evidence); a PII attribute's order key and lexical channel are inside the encrypted envelope or the attribute is not eligible for range rules (ER-ORDER-KEY-CHANNEL, ER-LEXICAL-CHANNEL).
obligations.title: Erasure reaches every protected copy

obligations.notes: Provisional product ruling (RULINGS Q24), flagged for Sam; the loop proceeds on it.
obligations.statement: The erasure ledger is kept apart from the data; a rebuild after erasure (ER-REBUILD) and a restore from a pre-erasure backup (ER-RESTORE-PRE-BACKUP) both replay it, so every read afterwards returns the ErasedValue marker and OBS-ERASURE-SCAN of the restored copy is clean.
obligations.title: Restore and rebuild re-apply the erasure ledger

obligations.statement: Per COMPOSITION eligibility (RULINGS Q31d): an index serves basis B only when its watermark, a fully resolved prefix, has reached B in B's epoch (CO-EPOCH-MISMATCH), C1's conditions hold, it can reconstruct B (a current-only index only inside the validity interval of every attribute read, CO-RECONSTRUCT-OUTSIDE-VALIDITY) and it has applied every published erasure (CO-ERASURE-FRONTIER); a read with no eligible index waits at most T-WATERMARK-WAIT-MS (CO-WATERMARK-WAIT) and then routes to an eligible fallback (CO-WATERMARK-FALLBACK) whose latency counts in the read's own latency (CO-FALLBACK-LATENCY-COUNTS); the receipt records the route and the surface language, a cross-language fallback is counted per surface (CO-FALLBACK-LANGUAGE), and fallbacks are reported as a share of reads per window (CO-FALLBACK-SHARE, OBS-WATERMARK); no index answers for a basis it is not eligible for (CO-NO-STALE-ANSWER); history and analytics trail asynchronously behind their watermarks (CO-ASYNC-HISTORY).
obligations.title: Reads are served only by an index eligible for their basis

obligations.statement: Per COMPOSITION ackOwnership (RULINGS Q31e, replacing Q28's ACK clause): the source of truth sends every ACK after its own publication (CO-ACK-AFTER-SOURCE-PUBLICATION, OBS-ACK-ORDER); the pull at the returned position is served by an index eligible for it, else by the fallback, so read-your-own-write is exact (CO-RYOW-ROUTED); during a current-index outage commits and ACKs continue and pulls fall back (CO-OUTAGE-ACKS-CONTINUE), and the index catches up from the feed through a bounded queue (CO-CATCHUP-BOUNDED-QUEUE). Per COMPOSITION fallbackEquivalence (RULINGS Q34b) and readGuarantees (RULINGS Q55c, provisional, flagged for Sam; supersedes Q50b), each serving surface the composition claims in the lane's language is tested against its own guarantee (CO-RYOW-PER-SURFACE): repository pulls read their own write by routing and fall back to the source with the replica down (CO-REPO-REPLICA-DOWN-FALLBACK); native answers report their basis (CO-NATIVE-REPORTS-BASIS), are never below a basis token (CO-NATIVE-BASIS-TOKEN-WAIT) or fail with E-BASIS-NOT-AVAILABLE after the request deadline (CO-NATIVE-BASIS-NOT-AVAILABLE), answer at the replica's watermark without a token (CO-NATIVE-NO-TOKEN-WATERMARK) and fail with E-REPLICA-UNAVAILABLE with the replica down (CO-NATIVE-REPLICA-UNAVAILABLE); no surface presents an answer as at a basis it was not computed at (CO-NO-FALSE-BASIS). Per COMPOSITION readGuarantees native (RULINGS Q58a, provisional, flagged for Sam; supersedes Q55c's native half): native queries go only through the Triplex facade (CO-FACADE-ONLY); an after: token waits for the replica marker within the deadline, then fails with E-BASIS-NOT-AVAILABLE {required, observed, replica} (CO-NATIVE-AFTER-TOKEN); an at: token is exact (CO-NATIVE-AT-EXACT) or fails with E-BASIS-NOT-RECONSTRUCTIBLE (CO-NATIVE-AT-NOT-RECONSTRUCTIBLE); a session sends its high-water mark as an implicit after (CO-SESSION-HIGH-WATER); every answer carries {basis: {low, high}, route} (CO-ANSWER-BASIS-RANGE-ROUTE); the default deadline is 2 s (CO-NATIVE-DEFAULT-DEADLINE). Per V-P2Q (RULINGS Q62a): Datalog and executor reads inside a transaction wait for the replica to reach the transaction's source position or fail typed (CO-EXECUTOR-IN-TX-WAITS-OR-TYPED), and executor reads are scope-wide in the compare-and-set read set (CO-EXECUTOR-READS-IN-CAS-SET); after a replica regression the real marker is read with the answer and nothing is answered below the basis (CO-REPLICA-REGRESSION-REAL-MARKER); a pull beyond the resolved prefix waits or fails with E-BASIS-NOT-AVAILABLE, on A0 too (CO-PULL-BEYOND-PREFIX-TYPED); during an outage pulls and retraction-target reads fall back to the log or fail with E-REPLICA-UNAVAILABLE (CO-OUTAGE-PULL-FALLBACK, CO-OUTAGE-RETRACTION-TARGET-FALLBACK). Per RULINGS Q67c: single-request surfaces read the replica marker in the same request as the answer, and multi-request surfaces (Datalog, executor) use replica incarnation fencing, accepting an answer only if (incarnation, marker) is equal before and after, the reset-during-query interleaving being an independently authored case (CO-RESET-DURING-QUERY); per RULINGS Q67h every such error has one representation, _tag BasisNotAvailable or ReplicaUnavailable with {required, observed, replica} and an optional cause (CO-TYPED-ERROR-SHAPE); both cases' manifests stay null until the design is built; a stale fallback is rejected (CO-STALE-FALLBACK-REJECTED); a cross-language fallback recipe is bound to the same semantic query identity (parameters, basis, meaning) and the same oracle answer (CO-CROSS-LANGUAGE-RECIPE-IDENTITY), with total request latency and language attribution recorded.
obligations.title: ACK after source publication; read-your-own-write by routing

obligations.statement: Per POSITION: a position is (stream, epoch, offset, ordinal), ordered lexicographically and not necessarily dense (PO-LEXICOGRAPHIC-ORDER); several Triplex transacts in one engine transaction take consecutive ordinals at one offset, assigned atomically with their assertions and the subject compare-and-set (PO-NESTED-CUTS-DENSE); a watermark is a fully resolved prefix and every aborted offset is listed in the feed's resolution stream (PO-ABORTED-LISTED); O-REPLAY sorts by coordinate and assigns its own dense ordinals for cuts (PO-ORACLE-DENSE-ORDINALS). Every composition, A0 included, passes the four falsifiers FX-NESTED-CUTS, FX-ABORT-GAP, FX-CRASH-APPEND-RESOLUTION and FX-RESUME-AT-ABORT-GAP before any comparative or promotion claim (GATE-POSITION, RULINGS Q38a); a dense allocator passes them cheaply, and no allowlist exempts it (OUTSIDE_BLOCK_MUTATION_FIXTURE, mutant M-WITHTRANSACTION-REBIND).
obligations.title: Positions are totally ordered coordinates with a fully resolved watermark

obligations.statement: Per POSITION binding (RULINGS Q51c), on both lanes: a transaction's position is bound only after the source of truth publishes it (PO-BOUND-AFTER-PUBLICATION); no adapter returns a placeholder position (PO-NO-PLACEHOLDER); one engine transaction holds more than 8 Triplex transacts with every ordinal distinct (PO-NO-ORDINAL-LIMIT); positions compare as opaque values in the (stream, epoch, offset, ordinal) order (PO-OPAQUE-TOTAL-ORDER).
obligations.title: Positions are bound after publication as opaque, totally ordered values

obligations.statement: V-D01 has independently reviewed W0's SPEC.md, releases and golden cases and every W0_PIN hash is pinned in this contract (W0-COV-REVIEW-PINNED; a null pin fails closed, GATE-W0); over the frozen trace at the 100k rung O-DOMAIN finds that R2 changes the outputs of at least W0-R2-CHANGED-SHARE of in-scope subjects (W0-COV-R2-CHANGED), every rule fires for at least W0-RULE-FIRE-SHARE of subjects (W0-COV-RULE-FIRES), worker-to-location fanout follows Zipf s = W0-LOCATION-ZIPF-S over W0-LOCATIONS-100K locations (W0-COV-LOCATION-FANOUT), and at least W0-MULTI-WORK-ITEM-SHARE of evaluations produce three or more work items (W0-COV-MULTI-WORK-ITEMS); world sizes follow P4's buckets through ballast (W0-COV-BALLAST-BUCKETS), the wage floor is two hops deep (W0-COV-TWO-HOP), R3 reaches its subjects through the reverse two-hop index with affected and changed subjects stated separately (W0-COV-R3-SCOPED), and O-DOMAIN reproduces the population fingerprint (W0-COV-FINGERPRINT) (RULINGS Q40, Q44).
obligations.title: W0 is reviewed, pinned and meets its frozen coverage floors

obligations.statement: Per ERASURE journalCommit and idempotence (RULINGS Q49a, Q49b): an erasure commit has a position, a txId, a record in transactions() and its own :_tx/ facts, and its changes list only identities (entity, attribute, assertion ids), never values (ER-COMMIT-JOURNAL-IDENTITY-ONLY); it is also written to the erasure ledger kept apart from the data, which restore and rebuild replay (ER-COMMIT-LEDGER); earlier transactions' :_tx/change facts for erased values show the ErasedValue marker (ER-EARLIER-CHANGE-MARKER); the first erasure of an identity sets erasedAt and erasing it again changes nothing (ER-IDEMPOTENT-REERASE); an erase that matches nothing (a well-formed selector with no assertions to erase) still commits a journal record with an empty change list (ER-EMPTY-ERASURE-RECORD); an erase naming an unknown target or id is E-INVALID-VALUE (ER-ERASE-UNKNOWN-TARGET, RULINGS Q56a); erase accepts retract's selectors, {id: ...} included (ER-ERASE-BY-ID, Q56f); retracting an already erased assertion commits and history shows the marker with the retraction's time (ER-RETRACT-AFTER-ERASE, Q56g); all values are synthetic (ERASURE syntheticData, Q56h).
obligations.title: An erasure commit is an ordinary, idempotent journal transaction

obligations.notes: Provisional product ruling (RULINGS Q24), flagged for Sam; the loop proceeds on it.
obligations.statement: Per ERASURE queries (RULINGS Q49c, provisional under the Q24 flag for Sam), on the repository, the native surface in the lane language and the raw recipes: an erased value is present with no readable value; it matches no value predicate (equality, inequality, range, pattern), so a filter never selects or rejects a subject by it (ER-PREDICATE-NO-MATCH); SUM, AVG, MIN and MAX skip it while COUNT of assertions counts it (ER-AGGREGATE-SKIP-COUNT); ORDER BY places erased markers last, in a deterministic order by assertion id (ER-ORDER-MARKERS-LAST); grouping puts all erased values of an attribute in one group keyed by the marker (ER-GROUP-ONE-MARKER); Unique ignores erased values (ER-UNIQUE-IGNORES); an erased reference cannot be followed and an include returns the marker (ER-REFERENCE-MARKER). Per ERASURE presence (RULINGS Q56b to Q56e): a card-one attribute with a readable and an erased value conflicts with E-CONFLICTING-VALUES (ER-CARD-ONE-READABLE-AND-ERASED), also when the readable value equals what the erased support held (ER-EQUAL-SUPPORT-ERASED-CONFLICTS); card-many markers follow the readable elements by assertion id (ER-CARD-MANY-MARKERS-LAST); Required is satisfied by an erased value (ER-REQUIRED-SATISFIED).
obligations.title: Erased values give deterministic query answers

obligations.notes: Provisional product ruling (RULINGS Q24), flagged for Sam; the loop proceeds on it.
obligations.statement: Per ERASURE queriesResidual, inFlight and commandShape (RULINGS Q52, provisional under the Q24 flag for Sam): a count of distinct values counts an attribute's erased values as one value (ER-COUNT-DISTINCT-MARKER, Q52a); ORDER BY puts readable values, then erased markers by assertion id, then missing values, in both directions (ER-ORDER-ERASED-THEN-MISSING, Q52b); a marker group reports the earliest erasedAt (ER-GROUP-EARLIEST-ERASEDAT, Q52c); an erased reference takes no part in reference constraints (ER-REFERENCE-CONSTRAINT-SKIPPED, Q52d); a read in flight across a commit erasing several values sees all old values or all markers, never a mix (ER-INFLIGHT-ALL-OR-NONE, Q52e); toDecimal(json, p, s, rounding) applies the named mode to the as-written reading and, without a rounding argument, excess digits are E-DECIMAL-FRACTION (DR-JSON-CONVERT-ROUNDING, Q52f); erasure is not an op and an erase mixed with other operations or given preconditions is a typed invalid-command error (ER-ERASE-COMMAND-SHAPE, Q52g); a read that started before n in-flight erasure commits sees one of the n + 1 prefixes (ER-INFLIGHT-PREFIXES, Q66a); a continuation cursor keeps its page's erasure prefix (ER-CURSOR-ERASURE-PREFIX, Q66b). O-REPLAY 0.4.1 refuses these shapes (ORACLE_REFUSALS q52-shapes), so this obligation stays blocked until 0.4.2 is accepted.
obligations.title: The Q52 shapes the pinned oracle does not model yet

obligations.notes: Provisional product ruling (RULINGS Q24), flagged for Sam; the loop proceeds on it.

obligations.statement: Every receipt binds the four assignments (source, current, history, analytics) with image digest, configuration hash and slot each, every replication edge (feed consumer source hash, translation generation) and the serving index's watermark at every read (CO-RECEIPT-BINDS-ALL, VA14); engine-scope keys derive from the assignment of the obligation's layer, never from engineOfLane (CO-SCOPE-KEY-FROM-ASSIGNMENT).
obligations.title: Receipts bind the whole composition

obligations.statement: The evaluator ships every EVALUATOR_COUNTEREXAMPLES receipt set and judges each OPEN, and every EVALUATOR_POSITIVE_FIXTURES receipt set and judges each CLOSED (O-CONTRACT); both catalogs cover every closure rule any obligation uses, so an evaluator that always answers OPEN, or always CLOSED, fails (RULINGS Q26, Q31k).
obligations.title: Incomplete receipts cannot close an obligation

obligations.statement: At P-YEAR-ONE one deployment holds the SCALE_POPULATION year-one population (10m entities, 100m active domain facts, at least 150M retained facts, tenants and strata as specified) written through public writes; every stratum and separate count matches independent count queries (OBS-SCALE-COUNT) and O-REPLAY analytic counts. This is the size the priorities are measured at, not a target in itself.
obligations.title: The year-one measurement population exists and is counted

obligations.statement: Rungs 10k, 100k, 1m and 10m subjects are admitted in order; each passes S.correctness.query-families at its own rung before the next is admitted.
obligations.title: Each rung passes before the next opens

obligations.statement: At every rung of P-RUNGS the query families (point, selective filter, join, anti-join, recursion, aggregate, historical, interval, pagination, subject pull) run on at least T-SAMPLES-PER-FAMILY samples with at least T-SAMPLES-PER-STRATUM in every applicable stratum plus complete-count queries, on the repository and in the lane language, all equal to O-REPLAY.
obligations.title: Query families correct at every rung

obligations.statement: Every rung is admitted with a peak forecast (rebuild overlap, delta growth, pre-GC growth, WAL, log, checkpoints, backups, replay, host clients); observed peaks stay within it (OBS-RESOURCE); an over-budget rung is BLOCKED_CAPACITY and stays open.
obligations.title: Runs fit the admitted envelope

obligations.statement: At every rung: bytes per entity and fact, write amplification per component (BUDGET_COMPONENTS), history separately, ingest rate, rebuild or compaction time, restart time, peak RSS per owner, peak disk.
obligations.title: Size and cost metrics are measured and reported separately

obligations.statement: Compaction, index rebuild and projection maintenance at P-YEAR-ONE complete; reads during and after equal O-REPLAY.
obligations.title: Maintenance at year one keeps reads correct

obligations.statement: An engine restart at P-YEAR-ONE becomes available within the recorded time and every sampled old cut re-reads identically.
obligations.title: Restart at year one

obligations.statement: At every rung the integrated candidate's complete-path cost (BUDGET_COMPONENTS, including log, broker and verification) and its NS measurements stay inside budgets.json, which is frozen before candidates, compared cumulatively against the frozen A0 control at the same rung.
obligations.title: The integrated candidate stays inside frozen budgets

OBS-ACK-ORDER.verdict: PASS iff the source of truth sent every ACK, tAck >= tSourcePublished for every commit, and every pull at a returned position was served by an eligible index or the fallback

OBS-AVAILABILITY.verdict: PASS iff a write and a read both succeed at some t <= tFailure + T-AVAIL-WINDOW-MS with no manual restart event

OBS-CANCEL.verdict: PASS iff callerError matches E-CANCELLED or E-TIMEOUT as the case pins, transportAck observed, the request id absent from every engine sample after tDrained with tDrained - tCancelRequested <= T-DRAIN-MS, sample gaps <= 1000 ms over [tCancelRequested, tDrained + 5000 ms], and the reuse query on the same connection succeeds

OBS-CONNECTIONS.verdict: PASS iff every sample <= declared max and the count equals baseline within T-CONN-RELEASE-MS after tClose

OBS-ERASURE-SCAN.verdict: PASS iff every PROTECTED_COPY_INVENTORY location of the lane is scanned after the erasure published and shows zero plaintext and zero derived-channel hits, or every surviving copy there is shown to be encrypted only under the destroyed per-subject key (key exclusivity, RULINGS Q31f)

OBS-FAULT-TRANSITIONS.verdict: the last witnessed transition is the last one whose durable evidence is present after the crash

OBS-MAINTENANCE.verdict: events present; lag statistics against the named threshold

OBS-NO-MUTATION.verdict: PASS iff the engine's committed-transaction or update counter is unchanged across the read

OBS-PREABORT.verdict: PASS iff zero engine statements carry the request id over the full coverage window

OBS-RESOURCE.verdict: PASS iff every peak <= forecast <= envelope (and <= T-PLANNER-MEM-BYTES where named)

OBS-SCALE-COUNT.verdict: PASS iff the count query's answer equals O-REPLAY's analytic count

OBS-SCRATCH.verdict: PASS iff countAfter = countBefore for every scratch relation and every unknown working outcome is resolved

OBS-WATERMARK.verdict: PASS iff no read was answered by an index that was not eligible (COMPOSITION eligibility: watermark in the basis epoch, C1, reconstructability, erasure frontier), every wait before routing is within T-WATERMARK-WAIT-MS, every route and its surface language is recorded, and the fallback latency is inside the read's measured latency

OBS-WORK.verdict: ratio of work units between the compared operations, evaluated against the named witness threshold

oracleAnswerRule: the evaluator runs the runner's argv with {case} replaced by the path of the pinned case input (and {mode} by the mode where the argv names it) in a directory holding only the pinned oracle files; exit 2, or X-NOT-MODELED on stdout or stderr, is a refusal; any other nonzero exit is an oracle error; neither is ever PASS; on exit 0 stdout is one canonical JSON document (UTF-8, key-sorted, the exact bytes of its own canonical form after one trailing newline is removed), and for O-REPLAY the expected answer is the object of the report's commandOutcomes, state and queries members, the report's own identity and verdict fields (format, oracle, caseId, caseSha256, lane, verdict, divergedAtCommand, receiptConsistency, rulesInEffect, reservedNamespaces) not being part of it; a case input given to the oracle carries no expectations of its own (RULINGS Q61c)

outbox.atomicUnit: per subject, the basis guard, retirement state, publication sequence, latest published payload and the outbox records are persisted in one atomic write under the subject's compare-and-set; the guard advances on empty and unchanged evaluations too (RULINGS Q42c)
outbox.atomicity: publication state (sequence and latest published payload) is persisted atomically with its outbox record
outbox.basisOrder: per subject the outbox applies an evaluation only if its basis is newer than the last applied one: greater basis.tx, or equal tx with a valid time not earlier; an older-basis evaluation publishes nothing (RULINGS Q40d)

cases.OB-ATOMIC-STATE: a crash between the outbox record and its publication state is impossible: both or neither are visible
cases.OB-CORRECTION-REVERT: a correction that reverts a payload to its previous value publishes a new sequence (RULINGS Q40c)
cases.OB-CRASH-BEFORE-DELIVERY: crash after the outbox record and publication state commit but before delivery: replay delivers the same (id, publication sequence) exactly once
cases.OB-OLDER-BASIS-NO-DELIVERY: a newer-basis R2 evaluation followed by an older-basis R1 evaluation yields no delivery (RULINGS Q40d)
cases.OB-PREVIEW-NOT-PUBLISHED: preview (GS.11) and past-valid-time audit evaluations are never passed to publish (RULINGS Q44c)
cases.OB-RELEASE-ROLLBACK: activate R1, R2, R1 over unchanged business facts: three deliveries with sequences 1, 2, 3 and payloads 1650, 1700, 1650
cases.OB-RETIREMENT-REAPPEAR: a work item that disappears and later reappears with the same payload publishes a new sequence (a second FNC notice is delivered, RULINGS Q40h)
cases.OB-UNCHANGED-ACTIVATION-RECOVERY: an activation that leaves the payload unchanged while an earlier delivery is still unacknowledged after a crash: nothing new is published and the pending delivery replays with its original identity

outbox.contentVersion: hashes (release, inputs, payload); recorded, never the delivery identity
outbox.liveOnly: a delivery's subject comes from the evaluation record; only live reconciles at the current basis are passed to publish; previews (GS.11) and past-valid-time audit evaluations never are (RULINGS Q44c)
outbox.operations: W0 defines publish(state, evaluations) -> {deliveries, state} and receive(state, deliveries) -> state as pure operations so O-DOMAIN gives the expected outbox and receiver state (RULINGS Q40c, Q42b)
outbox.publishRule: per id the sequence starts at 1; publish (id, seq + 1) when the id was never published, when the payload's canonical bytes differ from the latest published payload, or when the id reappears after a recorded retirement (even with an unchanged payload); version is content identity only (RULINGS Q40c, Q40h)
outbox.receivers: receivers apply deliveries per id by publication sequence: a state projection records the highest sequence applied and ignores any lower one (never regresses); an effect that needs every transition processes sequences in order and recovers gaps from the outbox before applying a later one; receiver deduplication is persisted atomically with the receiver's state or effect, or the recipient is idempotent by (id, seq); receivers exist from the first publication or are seeded with a state snapshot (RULINGS Q42b, Q44d)
outbox.recovery: unacknowledged deliveries survive crashes and replay with their original identity
outbox.retirement: when a work item id disappears from a subject's outputs, the outbox records its retirement; a later reappearance publishes a new sequence even if the payload equals the last published one (RULINGS Q40h)
outbox.sequence: durable per work-item id; increments when the payload to publish differs from the latest published payload for that id, so R1 to R2 to R1 publishes three deliveries (1650, 1700, 1650) and the receiver never suppresses the return
outbox.sweepFrames: provisional: a sweep page may publish up to 64 results in one frame: one atomic outbox commit per frame, each result its own work item with its own delivery identity (RULINGS Q68c, Q38f)

rulings.ruling: The ten goals stay on both lanes. Performance is measured as Sam's five priorities P1 to P5 on the fixed writer trace, with provisional bars that calibration may tighten and only Sam may loosen; the 20 golden scenarios are part of done; Sam's must-haves are requirements per engine (native or documented workaround with its own passing tests), never knockout gates; year-one size (10m entities, 100m active facts, retained history) is the measurement size, not a target in itself.

Exact storage and round trip for every value kind in use; order-preserving comparison for any attribute used in a range rule; a hard error, never silent conversion, for any value the engine cannot hold; integer range of at least 2^53; arithmetic over many rows only where a projection needs it. Arithmetic runs in the TypeScript kernel per subject; money is a scaled integer or an order-preserving decimal string; never floats for business values. The full signed 64-bit range is not required.

selectorSemantics: An obligation's cases are a list of {set, select}. select is a list of tags or named required case ids; 'all' selects every case of the set.
