wireRules.rule: a user-supplied JSON value containing -0, a non-finite number, or a number that does not read back as written (its shortest round-trip binary64 rendering differs from the given text in canonical form, RULINGS Q33a: 0.1 accepted, 9007199254740993 rejected) is rejected at every qualified write route with E-INEXACT-JSON-NUMBER (InvalidTripleError / invalid-value, detail inexact-json-number), never normalized; the guard runs before CanonicalJson, whose canonical identity is unchanged; approximateNumbers: reject applies recursively inside List and Struct; the guard applies to user JSON only: JSON that Triplex generates (journal changes, metadata) never passes through it, and the journal encodes typed values losslessly, so a number -0 assertion commits, journals, replays and reads back bit-exact (RULINGS Q34c, AMB-04)
an instant given as -0 is rejected with E-NEGATIVE-ZERO-INSTANT (NoNegativeZero), never turned into 0

ProjectionSpec pins the XTDB encodings F02 proved exact: card-many DOUBLE and integer lists are written as ARRAY[CAST(? AS <type>) ...], never as one JSON parameter; date and instant are read as text, never through the driver's TIMESTAMPTZ decoding; any other encoding fails the projection check

a QLever binary64 shadow counts as exact only if it is not -0 and parsing its %.13g rendering returns the same bits; integers only within +/-2^59; otherwise the lexical channel is authoritative and the shadow is flagged inexact (coarse pruning only, never an answer)
the ProjectionSpec integer range rule is narrowed to its safe-integer domain [-(2^53-1), 2^53-1] (cosmetic)

workloadIdentity.appliesTo: obligations whose closure rules include CR-NS or CR-GS only; correctness obligations carry no workload identity (RULINGS Q61g)
workloadIdentity.placement: each arm's placement {slot, cpuset, cpus} is separate from the shared workload identity; slots are per arm; a duet needs equal capacity, equal regime and disjoint cpusets; under cpusets the per-core denominator is the cpuset size (RULINGS Q67g)
workloadIdentity.rule: every measurement and control receipt carries workload {generatorSourceSha256 (trace generator hash), seed, offerScheduleSha256, window [from, to] with 0 <= from < to, slot (the source assignment's slot)}, every field present, typed and nonempty; a control matches a measurement only when the two workload identities are equal field by field; a missing field never matches a missing field (RULINGS Q47b)

worldW0.affectedSet: the expected affected set of a transaction is the subjects whose static read set contains a changed fact; static read sets over-approximate and never miss (RULINGS Q36e)
worldW0.ballast: rule-neutral ballast (owned answer entities <S>/ans:k with field and value text no rule reads, and a reference chain deep enough for 3 to 6 hops) sizes each world from P4's frozen buckets (50% 50-200 facts, 35% 201-800, 15% 801-2,000; a world may fall up to 2 facts below its bucket); trace commands use W0 and ballast attributes only, other attributes stay E_UNKNOWN; a ballast write affects nobody (RULINGS Q40a, Q44a)
worldW0.fanout: work-location fanout is a seeded Zipf with s = 0.5 over 2,000 locations at the 100k rung (largest location about 1,100 workers, mean 50); other rungs keep N / 50 locations with the same s; only the 100k numbers are frozen floors (RULINGS Q36g, Q36h)
worldW0.generator: every draw field is named (including the passport expiry draw); the population fingerprint is pinned once O-DOMAIN's independent generator reproduces V-D01's, using SPEC 12.7's exact recipe (RULINGS Q40g, Q44a)
worldW0.implementations: the TypeScript reference kernel the drivers call, and O-DOMAIN, an independent stdlib-only Python oracle giving expected next tasks, obligations with due times, work items and effect traces from the same command stream
worldW0.misreadingCases: every case V-D01 lists as must-add and should-add is in W0's case set (RULINGS Q40e, Q44a)
worldW0.nextEdit: none pending for W0; O-DOMAIN's next version adds unit tests for [1} (syntax error) and a duplicate key after the second member (V-D01c D1); its reading id A11 collides with W0-1.1.2's A11 (V-D01c D2, documentation only)
worldW0.positionOrdinal: positions in W0 are the 1-based dense ordinal of committed Triplex transacts in the tenant's source-of-truth stream, in coordinate order, supplied identically to the kernel and to O-DOMAIN (RULINGS Q40f)
worldW0.previewActivation: plan-impact preview (GS.11) and activation (GS.10) are compared at one common input basis (GS-10-11-COMMON-BASIS), never at different bases
worldW0.readings: SPEC 1.1.2 states the readings A01 to A15 as clarifications, each with a golden case (A10 exercised by the population): A01 to A10 from EXP-D01c (RULINGS Q53) and A11 to A15 from EXP-D01b (RULINGS Q57): A11 NaN, Infinity and -Infinity are W0.E_SHAPE, extending A01; A12 an integer token over 4,300 digits is still an integer token (E_VALUE for a value, E_BASIS for a tx), and implementations must not fail on their integer-parsing limits; A13 any nesting depth is a valid JSON value, then E_VALUE, and implementations must not fail on recursion limits; A14 strings order by Unicode code point, which equals UTF-8 byte order, for object keys and the sorts of items, subjects, effects and projection and the basis guard's validTime comparison, escapes following A07; A15 inconsistent receiver snapshots keep their entries as given, re-sorted stably by seq, only seq = done + 1 releases, and entries at or below done and the second of two duplicates stay waiting. Beside A12 (V-D01e N1): publish and receive integers have no upper bound; W0-1.1.1 stated none either, so no meaning changed. None of the readings changes a case of W0-1.1.1, a release or the fingerprint
worldW0.releaseR3: R3 is a scoped release: OT threshold 2,700 minutes only for placements whose location's jurisdiction is in a listed set (about 10% of jurisdictions), reached through the reverse two-hop dependency index; the scope is part of the release's content hash; expected affected subjects and changed subjects are stated separately; plus a runtime-outcome attribute and population facts with later valid-from dates (RULINGS Q40i, Q44b)
worldW0.releases: two releases R1 and R2; R2 changes three requirements; releases are content-addressed and activation is a fact
worldW0.role: a small frozen synthetic world definition used by every scenario, the P5 sweep and the P3 dependency rules; it stands in for Onboarded's real world definition and is not a Triplex product feature
rules: I-9 Section 1 task with a due time
I-9 Section 2 task with a due time
pay rate at or above the work location's minimum wage (a shared referenced entity)
worldW0.twoHopFloor: the wage floor is S.location -> L.jurisdiction -> J.stateMinWageCents (R2's local floor stays on L), so the dependency index follows two references; cases: a jurisdiction wage write, re-pointing (L, jurisdiction), and the R1/R2 split at that depth (RULINGS Q40b)

worldW0.witnesses: every scenario carries positive witnesses (subjects that must change) and negative witnesses (subjects that must not)
worldW0.workItemIdentity: a work item's id is SHA-256 over canonical JSON of (subject, rule, kind, key) only; its content version hashes (release hash, input positions, payload) and is not the delivery identity; each id carries a durable publication sequence that increments whenever the payload to publish differs from the latest published payload for that id, and the outbox delivery key is (id, publication sequence); an activation that leaves the payload equal to the latest published one publishes nothing (early cutoff); duplicate-effect checks count by delivery key (RULINGS Q36a, Q38f)
